title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays

concept.title: Binary search for the right split
body: The median splits the merged data into a left half and a right half of (almost) equal size. You can find that split **without merging**: cut array `a` at position `i` and array `b` at position `j = half - i`, where `half = (n + m + 1) // 2`. The cut is correct when everything on the left is at most everything on the right. As both arrays are sorted, this only needs two comparisons: `aLeft <= bRight` and `bLeft <= aRight`.

body.code:
i = (lo + hi) // 2;  j = half - i
aL = a[i-1] (or -inf)   aR = a[i] (or +inf)
bL = b[j-1] (or -inf)   bR = b[j] (or +inf)
if aL <= bR and bL <= aR:   # correct split
elif aL > bR: hi = i - 1    # took too many from a
else: lo = i + 1

body: Binary search over `i` in the shorter array takes O(log(min(n, m))). With a correct split, the middle values are `max(aL, bL)` and, for an even total, `min(aR, bR)`. To avoid fractions, this problem asks for **twice the median**.

statement: You are given two sorted arrays (increasing order). Consider all `n + m` numbers together in sorted order. Print **twice the median**: for an odd total that is twice the middle number, for an even total it is the sum of the two middle numbers. (This keeps the answer an integer.)
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` numbers of the first array.
The third line has the `m` numbers of the second array.

examples.note: Together: 1 2 3. The median is 2, so the answer is 4.
The middle numbers are 2 and 3, so the answer is 5 (the median is 2.5).

hints: Merging both arrays works but costs O(n + m); a binary search is faster.
Cut the shorter array at `i` and the other at `half - i`; the left parts together hold the smaller half.
The cut is right if `aL <= bR` and `bL <= aR`; otherwise move `i` left or right.

explanation: A correct cut puts the smaller half of all numbers on the left. Binary search on the cut of the shorter array finds it in O(log(min(n, m))) comparisons.
solution.complexity: Time O(log(min(n, m))) after reading, space O(1).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
b = list(map(int, input().split()))

x, y = a, b
if len(x) > len(y):
    x, y = y, x
nx, ny = len(x), len(y)
INF = 10**18
half = (nx + ny + 1) // 2
lo, hi = 0, nx
while lo <= hi:
    i = (lo + hi) // 2
    j = half - i
    aL = x[i - 1] if i > 0 else -INF
    aR = x[i] if i < nx else INF
    bL = y[j - 1] if j > 0 else -INF
    bR = y[j] if j < ny else INF
    if aL <= bR and bL <= aR:
        if (nx + ny) % 2 == 1:
            print(2 * max(aL, bL))
        else:
            print(max(aL, bL) + min(aR, bR))
        break
    elif aL > bR:
        hi = i - 1
    else:
        lo = i + 1
